newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL- S-E-BANKENS H1 PROFIT SEEN 11 PCT UP.
newsitem.headline: POLL- S-E-BANKENS H1 PROFIT SEEN 11 PCT UP.

text.p: Sweden's S-E-Banken was expected to post a profit after credit losses, of 3.02 billion crowns for the first half of 1997 compared to 2.72 billion crowns a year ago, a Reuters poll found on Friday.
Forecasts from 11 analysts varied between 2.62 million and 3.35 billion crowns.

Credit losses were expected to more than halve to 409 million crowns from 846 crowns a year earlier. For the full year, S-E-Banken's operating result was expected to fall to 5.63 billion crowns from 5.87 billion crowns.

Next year the bank was expected to show a higher profit of 5.70 billion crowns. The average forecast for calendar 1997 has increased five percent since Reuters's last poll that was taken before the bank's first quarter report.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Carnegie, Den Norske Bank, Enskilda, Goldman Sachs, James Capel, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Erik Penser, Swedbank, and Ohman.
S-E-Banken will release its report on Tuesday, August 12.
